subtopic: Caffeine, nicotine, alcohol and other substances
passage:
Gautam,
You asked what happened after the fest, so here it is, honestly. By eleven you were slurring, tripping over chairs, and when a senior bumped into you, you squared up and shouted in his face. I've never seen you like that. Then, suddenly, you went very sleepy, slumped on the steps, and it was hard to wake you. That scared me more than the shouting.
I didn't leave you. I kept you sitting up and kept talking to you. Nisha and I got you into an auto and back to the hostel, and I slept on the floor next to your bed. I'd decided that if you stopped responding, I'd call an ambulance, no question.
You're not in trouble with me. I just want you safe. Can we talk about it over chai?
Naveen

qa.q: How did Naveen and Nisha get Gautam back to the hostel?
qa.a: They got Gautam into an auto and back to the hostel.

qa.q: What scared Naveen most that night?
qa.a: Naveen was most frightened when Gautam went very sleepy and was hard to wake.

qa.q: Which of Naveen's actions were the caring ones?
qa.a: Staying with Gautam, keeping Gautam sitting up and talking, getting Gautam home, sleeping nearby and being ready to call an ambulance.

qa.q: How might Gautam feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Gautam may feel embarrassed and shaken, but also cared for, since Naveen says Gautam is not in trouble.

grounding: A friend sees slurring, aggression and heavy sleepiness, understands the danger, and stays, gets the person home and is ready to seek help.

subtopic: Caffeine, nicotine, alcohol and other substances
passage: Ira, you asked why I went so quiet at the party last week. It's because of last Diwali. My roommate Sameer drank a lot at a friend's place, and at first he was just loud and stumbling. Then he got angry at a guy over nothing and tried to shove him. I pulled him away and sat him outside. Twenty minutes later he wouldn't wake up properly. I shook his shoulder and said his name loudly. Nothing, just a groan. I didn't wait to see if he'd sleep it off. I called an ambulance and stayed with him till it came. The doctor said calling was the right thing. People laughed, and some still call me "Ambulance Harish". I don't care. Sameer's fine now. So when I see someone that drunk, yes, I go quiet. I'm watching them.

qa.q: Why does Harish go quiet around very drunk people now?
qa.a: Harish feels watchful and uneasy, remembering how Sameer stopped waking up properly.

qa.q: What choice did Harish make when Sameer wouldn't wake, and why was it right?
qa.a: Harish called an ambulance instead of waiting to see if Sameer would sleep it off, and stayed with him; the doctor said calling was right.

qa.q: How might Sameer feel about Harish's so-called overreaction now?
qa.a: Sameer would likely be grateful, since the call got him help when he could not wake up.

grounding: A friend notices stumbling, aggression and then unresponsiveness, stays with the person and calls for help.
